summary: Pre-market for the new week, the composite risk score stands at 43.18, a caution reading inside a goldilocks regime, and the past day left it essentially unchanged at -0.01 while the past week added 1.29. The stress is concentrated rather than broad: the macro block scores 65.36 on a real rate of 2.43 and a ten-year yield of 4.69, both near the top of their historical range, while the volatility block scores 25.15 with the VIX at 15.15 and liquidity and credit score 33.61 with high-yield spreads at 2.71. Cross-asset confirmation at 0.625 is the largest single contributor to the composite, and the signals behind it, gold bid 3.7176 percent higher against copper down 1.4356 percent and a firm broad dollar at 119.7034, describe a defensive rotation rather than an outright risk-off move. The macro backdrop is two-sided: payrolls have turned negative at -23.0 and continuing claims have risen to 1801000, yet headline inflation has cooled to 3.46353 and core to 2.56579. With no live session to price any of this, the coming week's US inflation and retail sales prints are the decisive catalysts, and the sectors feed is degraded, so theme-level readings in this brief should be treated as indicative only.

top_risk_drivers.claim: The macro block is the only stretched dimension at 65.36, driven by a ten-year real rate of 2.43 in the 99.04 percentile and a nominal ten-year yield of 4.69 in the 98.0 percentile.

Cross-asset confirmation at 0.625 is the largest single contribution to the composite at 7.5, with five of the eight production signals triggered: a firm dollar, real rate pressure, weaker copper, softer bitcoin and a gold bid.

Breadth is adequate but leadership is thin: only 0.1039 of the tracked universe is making new highs even though 0.6818 sits above its long-term moving average, and the new-highs shortfall alone adds 2.4212 to the score.
Reverse repo balances have drained to 1.45, a historically depleted level that contributes 3.4092 even while the aggregate liquidity and credit score stays low at 33.61.

The labour input has deteriorated: payrolls printed -23.0 against a positive prior reading, continuing claims rose to 1801000 and the participation rate slipped to 61.4, a combination that argues the goldilocks label rests on markets rather than on the real economy.

supporting_signals.claim: The dollar is a live risk channel: the broad index at 119.7034 keeps the dollar-strength signal triggered, and the advanced-economy index at 112.8987 confirms this is not a single-pair effect.

Volatility and credit are actively supportive rather than merely quiet: the VIX at 15.15 and realised volatility at 14.375 keep the volatility block at 25.15, while high-yield spreads at 2.71 and investment-grade spreads at 0.78 leave no credit stress to price.
The trend structure is intact, with the index proxy 9.9989 percent above its long-term moving average, a 52-week drawdown of 0.0 and three-month momentum of 5.6973 percent.

contradicting_signals.claim: Yields rose even as inflation cooled, the core tension in this fact set: the ten-year moved to 4.69 and the two-year to 4.25 while headline inflation eased to 3.46353 and core to 2.56579, so the real rate at 2.43 is being driven by the nominal leg rather than by an inflation scare.
The curve argues against a recession trade: the spread of the ten-year over the two-year is 0.44, comfortably positive, and the effective funds rate is anchored at 3.63.

Not all of the labour data is weak: the unemployment rate actually fell to 4.1 and initial claims at 199000 remain low by historical standards, so the payroll drop is not yet corroborated by the higher-frequency series.

what_changed_today: The composite score is effectively flat over the past day at -0.01 and higher by 1.29 over the past week, so the weekly drift did not extend into the latest reading.
Confidence in the reading is high at 0.9211 on full data quality and coverage of 0.93, but consistency remains the weak leg at 0.7457.
The sectors feed dropped to degraded while macro, equities, crypto, news, calendar and risk all remain fresh, so theme-level readings are the least reliable part of this brief.

Weekend flow was dominated by an inflation-turn narrative out of China and by a storage-versus-optics debate in the chip complex, both relayed second-hand through aggregator feeds rather than sourced first-party.
watch_next: US CPI is the first hard catalyst of the week and feeds directly into the real rate that dominates this score.
PPI and advance retail sales follow, and together they test whether the cooling in headline inflation is demand-led or merely a pass-through of fading import costs.
Watch whether the ten-year holds its recent range; a further rise with breakevens flat would push the real rate higher again and lift the macro block.
Watch the new-highs ratio for confirmation: breadth above the long-term average without new highs is the classic signature of a narrowing tape.
Watch the memory complex, where a negative theme print sits against strong mainland storage names; the divergence resolves one way or the other on the next full session.

bull_case.title: Bull case: disinflation lets real rates fall back
points: Headline inflation at 3.46353 and core at 2.56579 are both below their prior readings, and core PCE has eased to 3.28653.
Long-run inflation expectations stay anchored, with the five-year forward at 2.28 and the ten-year breakeven at 2.25, leaving room for the nominal leg to fall without a growth scare.
Credit is already positioned for that outcome, with high-yield spreads at 2.71 and investment-grade at 0.78.

base_case.title: Base case: caution persists on a macro-only imbalance
points: The composite holds near 43.18, with volatility at 25.15 and liquidity and credit at 33.61 offsetting a macro block at 65.36.
Cross-asset confirmation stays near 0.625, keeping the largest single contribution in place without escalating it.
Breadth stays adequate at 0.6818 above the long-term average while new highs remain thin at 0.1039.

bear_case.title: Bear case: rate pressure meets a weakening labour market
points: A hot inflation print revives rate-hike pricing while payrolls at -23.0 and continuing claims at 1801000 confirm the demand side is already cracking.
The real rate pushes above 2.43 and the macro block rises from 65.36, with no offset available because the VIX is already compressed at 15.15.
Narrow leadership gives way: the new-highs ratio at 0.1039 rolls over first and drags breadth below 0.6818.
